newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids gain again on weather, crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids gain again on weather, crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices continued to score modest gains Wednesday, as firmer crude and more heat in Florida and the Southeast supported values despite further weakness in gas, market sources said.

"The contract buyers (for utilities) have been out looking for oil, and Mexico is still searching around for (high sulphur) barrels," said one cash trader, noting the recent East Coast heat wave stirred much better demand.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent firmed almost 50 cents to about the $17 a barrel level on reports of a cargo sale late Tuesday at $17.05, traders said.
NYH July one percent paper rose another 15-20 cents to the low-$17 area on stronger NYMEX crude.
NYH 0.3 high pour held relatively steady in the $18.25 area, traders said.
High sulphurs in New York also gained, with 2.2 percent up a quarter to $15.00-25.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was 15 cents higher at about $15.50, boosted by reports of a prompt 100,000 barrel sale Tuesday at $15.50 (4 gravity material).

USG three percent rose 25 cents to about $13.75, helped by talk that Mexico was still looking for barrels and reports 50-60,000 barrels of prompt 2.75 percent (9 gravity, 350 vanadium) sold at $13.75, traders said.

New York city gate gas prices slipped three cents Wednesday to the high-$2.30s/mmBtu, or $14.99 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was down a similar amount to about $2.13/mmBtu, or $13.42 a barrel.
